What’s a good cost per lead in digital marketing?

Ava Digital · Updated 2026 · ~4 min read
Short answer: It varies widely — from ~$20–$50 for local services to $200–$1,000+ for B2B, legal, and finance. A “good” cost per lead is simply one where the lead’s value comfortably clears its cost — aim for a 3–5× return.

Typical ranges by industry

  • Local home services — ~$20–$75
  • Healthcare / dental — ~$50–$200
  • E-commerce — ~$10–$60
  • B2B / SaaS — ~$100–$500
  • Legal / finance — ~$250–$1,000+

What “good” really depends on

CPL alone is meaningless without two numbers: your average customer value and your close rate. A $300 lead is a bargain if you close 1 in 3 and each client is worth $5,000.

Find your target CPL

Target CPL = (customer value × close rate) ÷ your desired return. Then lower it with tighter targeting, better landing pages, and stronger offers.
